findings.title: fetchWorkspaceFiles retries cancelled reads forever, with no bound and no exit on unmount
findings.body: The old code retried a `CancelledError` once. The new `for (;;)` loop retries every cancellation. The loop has no attempt limit, and it does not check whether the view is still mounted or the session has changed. This PR makes cancellation routine, because the manifest query now takes the abort signal, and `useQuery` observers such as `SessionFileExplorer` and `SessionBranchSummary` share that query key. A cancelled read can therefore come back repeatedly. An awaiting caller (`resolvePaneFile` at line 2286, `revealResolvedWorkspaceFile` at line 2560) keeps issuing `fetchQuery` calls after the user has left the chat. If cancellation arrives immediately each time, for example from a repeated `cancelQueries` or a mocked rejection, the loop spins on microtasks and never yields. Consider a small fixed retry count (for example 2–3), then rethrow. Alternatively, check `isCancelledError` against a `cancelled` flag set on unmount or session change.
